methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $14M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
The ePlane Company is a Series B-stage transportation startup founded by Satya Chakravarthy, currently seeking to raise $40–50M on top of $14M+ already deployed. The broader transportation sector includes seven private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, DeepDrive among others) and no directly comparable public companies, limiting peer-based valuation anchors.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, as peer-median comparison was not feasible. The peer universe in transportation yielded no same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables meeting the three-datapoint threshold for statistical reliability. The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $14M total-raised proxy, consistent with Series B step-up conventions, implying a post-money valuation of $27M.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $23M (low), $27M (median), to $31M (high). This range reflects only one applicable method, introducing material sensitivity to the underlying stage-multiplier assumption. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer benchmarking, reliance on a single methodological input, and the company's pre-revenue or early-traction status within a capital-intensive sector. Investors should weigh this quantitative band against management execution risk and the company's technical and regulatory pathway.
